items.headline: CISA adds actively exploited N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label flaws to KEV catalog
items.summary: CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing active exploitation. One is CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 9.3), a server-side request forgery flaw tied to LDAP in N-able MailAssure. The other is a MONAI Label zero-day that reporting links to AI-agent-driven exploitation; its CVE ID was not available in the source excerpt.
items.importance_rationale: These are new KEV entries showing active exploitation, including an email-security product sold through MSPs.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that defenders should look for unexpected outbound LDAP or HTTP requests from MailAssure and for anomalous access to MONAI Label servers. No detection rule is linked.
items.recommended_action: Apply vendor fixes for MailAssure and MONAI Label right away, following KEV guidance. Then review logs for signs of compromise. Details on the MONAI issue are still limited.
items.model_importance_rationale: These are new KEV entries showing active exploitation, including an email-security product sold through MSPs.

kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

items.headline: Peninsula Energy halts trading after cyber incident at Wyoming uranium project
items.summary: Peninsula Energy told the ASX that a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming uranium project will temporarily affect operations. It has halted trading in its shares. The cause and scope have not been disclosed.
items.importance_rationale: An incident is disrupting operations at a US energy-sector organization, which meets the rubric for a major outage in a target industry.
items.detection_coverage_note: No TTPs were disclosed. Our assessment is to check visibility at the boundary between IT and OT.
items.recommended_action: Energy and mining operators should review how well their IT and OT networks are segmented and check their incident readiness. Watch for further disclosures from the company.
items.model_importance_rationale: An incident is disrupting operations at a US energy-sector organization, which meets the rubric for a major outage in a target industry.

items.importance_rationale: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high.
items.detection_coverage_note: No detection rules were provided. In our assessment, reviewing the platform's logs for unusual admin activity is advisable.

items.headline: Azure API Management Classic flaw exploited to steal stored customer credentials
items.summary: Microsoft warned that attackers exploited a vulnerability in Azure API Management Classic tiers to steal credentials stored in customer instances. Norway's NSM confirmed that victims include Norwegian energy firms Equinor and Skagerak Energi, as well as organisations in other sectors and countries.
items.importance_rationale: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that reviewing APIM activity logs, and checking for unusual use of backend credentials stored in APIM, is the most practical way to find misuse. The source names no detection rules.
items.recommended_action: Follow Microsoft's guidance for APIM Classic tiers, rotate all secrets and credentials stored in APIM instances, and review logs for unauthorised access to the backends they protect.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high
Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

items.headline: 13 malicious NuGet packages target .NET developers through fake job assessments
items.summary: Socket researchers found 13 malicious NuGet packages tied to fake developer job assessments. The packages use DLL side-loading, steal credentials and rely on GitHub-hosted malware infrastructure.

items.detection_coverage_note: Assessment: watch developer endpoints for DLL side-loading and for unusual outbound connections to GitHub during builds.
items.recommended_action: Block the identified packages, enforce allow-listed package sources, and warn developers about job-assessment lures.

items.headline: Okta links ShinyHunters-associated vishing cluster O-UNC-053 to new INCEPTION data leak site
items.summary: Okta Threat Intelligence assesses that O-UNC-053, a voice-phishing cluster previously linked to ShinyHunters, may have rebranded as INCEPTION and launched a new data leak site. The group calls targets to get them to enter credentials on phishing pages and approve authentication prompts. Okta presents the rebrand as a possibility, not a confirmed fact.
items.importance_rationale: This is an active vishing and extortion operation targeting enterprise identity, now with a new leak site.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment: IdP logs could flag MFA approvals and sign-ins from unusual devices or locations after helpdesk or user calls. The sources provide no detection rules.
items.recommended_action: Move to phishing-resistant MFA, tighten helpdesk identity checks, and watch for suspicious MFA approvals.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is an active vishing and extortion operation targeting enterprise identity, now with a new leak site.

items.headline: Unauthenticated SQL injection in WHMCS shopping cart can expose customer data and admin hashes
items.summary: WHMCS, a billing and automation platform used by many web hosting providers, disclosed a SQL injection in its shopping cart. An unauthenticated attacker could use it to pull customer records and administrator password hashes. Two other flaws that need a client login were disclosed at the same time, and the vendor has released fixes. No exploitation has been reported.
items.importance_rationale: An unauthenticated data-exposure flaw in a widely used hosting platform, with a vendor patch available. No exploitation has been reported.
items.detection_coverage_note: Assessment: WAF and web-log monitoring for SQL injection patterns on cart endpoints may help. No published rules were provided.
items.recommended_action: Apply the WHMCS updates now. Review cart access logs for injection attempts. Consider rotating admin credentials if exposure is suspected.
items.model_importance_rationale: An unauthenticated data-exposure flaw in a widely used hosting platform, with a vendor patch available. No exploitation has been reported.

items.headline: Critical unauthenticated buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers awaits vendor fix
items.summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-328-03 describes CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.8), a stack-based overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler on Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers up to version 5.4.0. Crafted POST requests can crash the webserver, and the advisory says code execution is possible in theory. A fix is planned for version 5.5.x. The advisory does not report any exploitation.
items.importance_rationale: This is a critical-severity ICS advisory for an unauthenticated network flaw, and no patch is available yet. No exploitation has been reported.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that defenders should monitor for unusual HTTP/S POST requests to the controller's CGI endpoints and for unexpected webserver restarts. None of the sources provide a detection rule.
items.recommended_action: Find all AK-SM 8xxA units and take them off the internet. Restrict access to them through a VPN, turn on Strict Mode, and apply version 5.5.x once it is released.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a critical-severity ICS advisory for an unauthenticated network flaw, and no patch is available yet. No exploitation has been reported.

items.headline: FCA warns UK financial firms to govern AI agent risks or face supervisory action
items.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said financial firms must maintain effective oversight and governance controls over AI agents as their use grows across the sector. The source frames this as a warning that firms which fail to address the risks may face action.

items.model_importance_rationale: This is regulator guidance and a warning, not a new binding rule with a set date. It still bears directly on UK financial firms.

items.headline: Project Zero shows .NET loading quirk bypassing Windows code integrity and VirtualBox hardening
items.summary: A Google Project Zero researcher described how a .NET Framework file-loading behaviour lets a local attacker run untrusted code past Windows code integrity. The same behaviour also bypassed Oracle VirtualBox process hardening on Windows hosts, tracked as CVE-2026-87268. The source does not report any exploitation in the wild.
items.importance_rationale: This is a local security-feature bypass in widely deployed Windows and .NET, with no reported exploitation.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment is that EDR telemetry on unusual .NET assembly loads into hardened processes may help. The source names no detection rules.
items.recommended_action: Check whether Microsoft and Oracle have released fixes, apply the VirtualBox update, and do not rely on code integrity as the only barrier against local code execution.
items.model_importance_rationale: This is a local security-feature bypass in widely deployed Windows and .NET, with no reported exploitation.

items.recommended_action: Look for unexpected VPN bridge or tunnelling software, especially binaries posing as monitoring tools. Attribution in the source is suspected, not confirmed.
items.model_importance_rationale: Threat research describing new evasion techniques. The source names no specific critical-infrastructure targets in the priority regions.

items.headline: Anthropic interviews at 58 companies examine how AI adoption is changing work and hiring
items.summary: Anthropic published research based on interviews with people at 58 companies that use Claude. Participants reported few layoffs but less hiring. They said AI delivered the most value when companies reorganized roles and workplaces around it. The study covers workforce effects, not security issues.
